### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5dbcc02b84d57b982444cdbd2516761d3419defe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `75c937cfa979bb77c35bab095718d149d0968d62`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #37183 (body, triage 7150888022 and 7185024000, claim 7189478405, os-dev report 7191594141), the PR #37540 body, the net diff against `origin/main` (one file, `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/data-commands.absent-database.integration.test.ts`, +58/-18), and the check-runs on the head. Every check-run that ran on the head passed, Test Core 1-10, Build Core, Type Check (all four), Lint (all), Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard and PR-body guards among them. The rest were skipped as opt-in or UI-only.

### ① Derived judgments

The change adds no accept set and no public surface. It touches only an integration test's hook layout, and the account in the PR body holds up.

- **Root cause, right.** On `main`, the `[#21552]` family's single `beforeAll` ran the family seed and then 40 CLI children in sequence (12 doors x 3 faces + 4 already-exit-zero) under one 480 s timeout. At the queue build's ~11.5 s per child, those 41 serial runs pass 480 s while each stays far under its own 120 s kill. The module-level hook had the same shape on a smaller scale: one seed plus 9 runs.
- **New shape, right.** There are 2 seed hooks, 3 per-command hooks, 12 per-door hooks and 1 already-exit-zero hook, each at `BATCH_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` = 150 s. The cli config sets only `sequence.sequencer`. Vitest 4.1.12 resolves `sequence.hooks ??= "stack"`, and the runner's `callSuiteHook` then awaits `beforeAll` hooks one at a time and stops at the first throw. So every seed finishes before the first batch that reads its database, and batches never overlap.
- **Cases unchanged, right.** All 54 are intact: [#21529] absent 7, control 6, family 12+12+1+12+4. No `it`, `it.each`, assertion or test name is in the diff, and there is no `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`.
- **Failure surfacing, right.** A non-zero exit still resolves as a `Run` with its `code`, and the asserting test checks `code` exactly as before. `runCli` rejects only on a spawn error or on the 120 s kill. `settleBatch` waits for every run, then throws one `Error` that joins every rejection message, so `allSettled` swallows nothing. A throw fails the hook, stops the later hooks and fails the suite's cases. That is how a rejection surfaced on `main` too, now with every failed run named instead of the first.
- **No shared-state collision, right.** Within a batch, two children (four in the already-exit-zero batch) read the absent path and at most one reads a booted database (`booted.db` or `family.db`). The booted databases are touched by one child at a time, in the same order as on `main`. The absent path is still asserted not to exist at the end, so a regression that creates it still fails. All children share one `mkdtemp` dir as cwd, a read-only artifact, the fixed `OS_SECRET_KEY` (no key is minted into home), `OS_TELEMETRY_DB=0`, and an env copy built per child. These are one-shot commands, and nothing in the migrate, secret or storage paths calls `listen()`. Nothing here adds shared state that the vitest workers running other files in parallel do not already share.
- **150 s margin, right.** Every child's kill timer starts when its hook starts, so a batch ends within about 120 s however loaded the shard is and however many children the batch holds. The other 30 s covers the SIGKILL and the rejection reaching the hook. Measured under contention, children ran about 12-14 s three at a time, and the slowest hook took 14.2 s. The seed hooks block on `spawnSync`, bounded by its own 120 s `timeout`.
- nit: the `settleBatch` doc says "no child outlives the hook that started it". When a run hits its 120 s kill, `runCli` rejects straight after `kill('SIGKILL')` and before `close`, so a killed child can still be exiting when the hook fails. This is harmless and the same as on `main`, but the sentence says more than the code guarantees.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right. The only file changed is a `*.integration.test.ts`. The dev searched `packages/cli/dist` and found 0 hits for the new identifiers, against a positive control, and Check Changeset passed. The `Clause-②: no` line on the PR body and the claim is right, since nothing published changes.

The test-budget header is right. The spawn count is corrected to 49 (9 + 36 + 4) and the door count to twelve, matching the file. On `main` the header still said 46 and eleven, written before `migrate unmapped-columns` was added. The 450 s stays: the old serial shape's CI readings justified it, and the new shape is shorter. The vitest-slices reader of the header is green in CI.
- nit: the line's derivation still cites the serial shape's runs. As the dev notes, it should be re-measured from the first CI readings of the new shape. No action is owed in this PR.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none.
- Out-of-scope findings: the ~6 s CLI spawn floor through `run-dev.js`, and the fact that the file's wall may not shrink on a runner with no spare cores. Both are cost observations, and both are recorded in the PR's Acceptance notes. Not filing them is right, since neither is a defect class.
- Deviations: the contention reading is an upper bound, not an equal-load comparison. This is acknowledged and does not change the bound argument.
- Gates: the two NOT MEASURED local gates (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n-coverage`) are answered by CI on the head.
- SQL push-down: no production code changes, so there is no new id materialisation or in-app join to check.
